name: omarchy-fred-ecosystem
description: Third-party packages Fred's Omarchy workstations run patched, and the software of his that depends on those patches

conventions.fork_branches: patch/<slug> per patch and patchset/<release-tag> integration branch, both off the upstream release tag the PKGBUILD builds; `fred` always points at the current patchset and is the fork's default branch
conventions.fork_tags: <release-tag>-fred.<N>, N bumped whenever the patch set changes (independent of pkgrel)
conventions.local_version: Arch's version with pkgrel <archrel>.<N>: outranks Arch's build of the same version, loses to any newer Arch build, so the patch retires itself
conventions.patches: exported from the fork with `omarchy-fred-ecosystem export <pkg>` (git format-patch, one file per commit, in order); builds stay tarball + patches
conventions.posting_upstream: see docs/agent-guides/upstream-engagement.md in omarchy-fred-config: agents never post on hyprwm/*; issue-first elsewhere with AI use disclosed

packages.name: gtk4
packages.summary: Wayland dmabuf format table: munmap of the wrong pointer crashed every GTK4 Wayland app on the second dmabuf feedback round

patches.subject: gdk/wayland: munmap the format table, not the formats array
patches.origin: backport of GTK MR !10166 (merged upstream; first release 4.23.3, also on gtk-4-22 so 4.22.5+)

packages.retires_when: Arch ships gtk4 >= 4.22.5 (but not 4.23.0-4.23.2) or >= 4.23.3; the pacman hook does the comparison

packages.name: aquamarine
packages.summary: Disable the KMS pipeline before tearing down a disconnected connector; without it a resume or hotplug can hand a still-active CRTC to another connector and every atomic commit fails (Fault D)

patches.subject: drm: disable KMS output before disconnect cleanup
patches.author: Nico Duldhardt (klaudworks) — cherry-picked from upstream PR #395 with authorship preserved

filed.state: closed 2026-09-09, unvouched author (not ours); tracking issue hyprwm/aquamarine#386

packages.retires_when: an Arch aquamarine release whose SDRMConnector::disconnect() disables KMS before the teardown (watch hyprwm/aquamarine#386); version unknown until it lands

packages.name: hyprland
packages.summary: Two fixes: a monitor that connects while DPMS is off stays dark, and an unchanged idle-inhibit re-evaluation (every focus change) no longer resets ext-idle-notify timers

patches.subject: Inherit the compositor-wide DPMS state when a monitor connects

filed.state: closed 2026-09-17 by bot (unvouched); not to be re-filed — hyprwm AI policy

patches.subject: Do not reset ext-idle-notify notifications when the inhibit state is unchanged

filed.state: not filed and not to be filed — hyprwm AI policy; draft kept in packages/hyprland/upstream-pr.md

packages.retires_when: an Arch hyprland release containing both fixes (onConnect() honours the compositor DPMS state; setInhibit() guards the unchanged case). If only one lands, drop that patch and rebuild as <arch>.1
packages.verify_binary: test "$(strings /usr/bin/Hyprland | grep -c 'connected while DPMS is off')" = 1 && test "$(strings /usr/bin/Hyprland | grep -c 'inhibit state unchanged')" = 1
packages.abi_note: same tarball, same GIT_COMMIT_HASH, so the plugin ABI string is unchanged and hyprbars keeps loading; never build from the fork's git tree

packages.name: omawrite
packages.summary: Five fixes the omawrite-review workflow depends on: in-window close button, always open the CLI file, a 'File removed' dialog that recovers and whose Reload works, no shortcuts-dialog binding loop, 80-column editor width

patches.subject: Add in-window close button to top-right corner
Always open an explicitly requested command-line file
Let "File removed" recover when the file comes back, and make Reload work
Stop the shortcuts dialog from reporting a binding loop on every launch
Expand editor max column width from 65 to 80 characters

packages.retires_when: Arch ships omawrite >= 0.5.1 with a native close button, reliable CLI opening, a working Reload in the 'File removed' dialog, a loop-free shortcuts dialog and >= 80-column width; otherwise rebase the stack onto the new release
